en: One kind of special form of grounding, you
could say, is Retrieval Augmented
Generation, or RAG. That's another core
concept to be aware of. And the idea behind
RAG is that you connect a model to certain
sources, to a database, for example,
and the software which runs the model, so
your custom AI agent or maybe ChatGPT, which
was connected to such a database,
That software
runs queries behind the scenes whenever you
send a prompt or a message to the agent.
And it searches that database for sources
automatically, sources that may seem
relevant to your query,
and injects these sources automatically into
your prompt and sends your prompt plus those
identified sources to the large language
model so that without you explicitly adding
those sources,
useful sources are added nonetheless to your
prompt. And therefore, as you learned, you
get a higher chance of getting a correct
output because the large language model now
generates its tokens not just on your
prompt, but instead on your prompt plus
those automatically loaded sources. If you
want to set up RAG, you need a software that
supports it. You may need to build your own
AI agent and you will need a a so-called
vector database, which is worth a separate
look.
